formatted.abraham1995sadri: Liju Abraham. A sociolinguistic survey of the Sadri-speaking people of India. Manuscript, 1995. Bibliographic details reported by Behera 2022, printed page 104. Behera printed page 18 attributes the Standard Sadri Brave Hunter text to Appendix C-11 of this manuscript. The manuscript has not been independently collated.
formatted.behera2022korwakodaku: Gangadhar Behera. A sociolinguistic profile of Korwa and Kodaku tribes in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, India. Technical Report 2022-014, SIL International, 2022. Fieldwork 2004–2005. Source-specific language and locality identities remain separate from speakers and test audiences. The Standard Sadri Brave Hunter text is reported from Abraham 1995 Appendix C-11, not independently collated. Birjia remains distinct from Birhor/Asuri/Korwa. Literal additions preserve field-transcription distinctions without inferred phonemic analysis; the legacy profile remains separate. New literal evidence uses the embedded text layer and original-page review; older OCR was a comparison aid, not installed transcription. Qualified introductory word-origin claims remain attributed commentary, not historical edges. Source conflicts and uncertain alignments are explicitly recorded. URL: https://www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/94564.
formatted.singh1994scheduledtribes: K. Suresh Singh. The scheduled tribes. Volume 3 of People of India. Anthropological Survey of India; Oxford University Press, Delhi, 1994. Bibliographic details reported by Behera 2022, printed page 104. Behera printed page 1 cites page 1826 for kor man and a plausible connection with the name Korwa, page 613 for dodawas earth diggers, and page 546 for Kodwa digger of the soil. The book has not been independently collated.
formatted.ctdp2002hillkorwa: Chhattisgarh Tribal Development Programme. Major tribes: Hill-Korwa (Pahari Korwa). 2002. Bibliographic details and historical URL reported by Behera 2022, printed page 104, which records access on 30 June 2006. The original website has not been independently collated. URL: http://cjtdp.nic.in/tribes.htm.
formatted.powercity_korba_ndc: Powercity Korba. The people of Korba: hilly Korwa. Undated authority labeled n.d.c by Behera 2022. Bibliographic details and historical URL are reported on printed page 104, with access dated June 30, 2006. Behera printed page 1 attributes the Kora womb origin myth to this source. The website has not been independently collated. URL: http://www.powercitykorba.com/people.html.
